chapter: Baton Rouge big band and New York
title: Standard Oil job as assistant stillman, homebrew, and the company band's duties
summary: He was imported to the plant for clarinet, worked on stills, joked about homebrew, and the band played parades, Mardi Gras and concerts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, let's see. Did you play full time with that Stand It All band? Oh, yeah. I was employed in the band that imported me there. Old man Webber heard me playing clarinet.
And he had me imported into the plant, you see. And you played every day there? No, no, no. No, no. Just… You were a still worker.
I was working on stills. I was an assistant stillman when I left there. Mm-hmm. Well, I guess those were good times to be working on a still. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm .
Mm-hmm . Well, I guess those were good times to be working on a still. In those days, you needed a still.
Well, all I had to do was I could go block away if I wanted to sit down and wash it. As long as it didn't blow up, it's all right.
Oh, I see. But y'all weren't making any moonshine. I think that's still just all stuff. He was pushing back to homebrew and forth in those days.

I'm homebrew, though. I made about two glasses. You and that bro made a batch. Me and that bro made us one batch and we put it in the chicken house. Oh, I let them bop, bop, bop, bop, bop, bop, bop. Went out there in the back quick. My whole brew was popping off one after the other. You made one batch and put it in the stove and put it in the oil wire and put it in the stove. It didn't like it. I'm trying it all right. You didn't have to play all the time. You would watch or steal it? No, we played mostly for just special games. You know what I mean?
Parades? I was saying, you played parades with that band? Mm-hmm.
Well, I played anything they wanted, but all heavy stuff, big heavy stuff. The orchestra, we played jazz music. With the whole band, we played nothing special, but gauges.
You played for dances with that big band ever? No, no, no.
No, I mean special gauges, but I mean like Mardi Gras and all this stuff like that. That's kind of stuff. We played a whole lot of concerts. We did a whole lot of concerts.
